questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and Correcting Statements

subQuestions.questionText:
The following statement does NOT apply to the marketing of agricultural products:
A. Marketing management is profit-orientated
B. Determines the needs of the consumers and supply accordingly
C. Focuses on the needs of the seller
D. Planning is long term, based on new products for future growth
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Focuses on the needs of the seller (2 marks)
Marketing focuses on the needs of the consumer. Focusing on the seller's needs describes the selling concept.

options.B: Determines the needs of the consumers and supply accordingly
options.C: Focuses on the needs of the seller
options.D: Planning is long term, based on new products for future growth

subQuestions.questionText:
The type of buyer who works for commission, buys cattle at a certain price and sells them at a higher price:
A. Retailer
B. Broker
C. Wholesaler
D. Processing company
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Broker (2 marks)
A broker (speculator/agent) buys and sells on behalf of others for a commission, aiming to profit from the price difference.

subQuestions.questionText:
ONE of the following is NOT a reason for price fixing:
A. Elimination of competition
B. Increasing profit margins
C. Selling the same product, at the same price, by different producers
D. Improves accessibility of a product for consumers
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Improves accessibility of a product for consumers (2 marks)
Price fixing benefits the producers who agree on the price, not consumers. It removes competition and raises profit margins.

options.C: Selling the same product, at the same price, by different producers
options.D: Improves accessibility of a product for consumers

subQuestions.questionText:
The following statements are reasons for drawing up a business plan:
(i) To determine whether it will be possible to implement the business idea successfully
(ii) For paying back the bank loan
(iii) To guide daily operations
(iv) To determine the financial needs of the business
Choose the CORRECT combination:
A. (i), (ii) and (iii)
B. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
C. (i), (iii) and (iv)
D. (i), (ii) and (iv)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - (i), (iii) and (iv) (2 marks)
Paying back a bank loan (ii) is not a reason for drawing up a business plan. The plan tests feasibility, guides operations and determines financial needs.

subQuestions.questionText:
All the economic inputs that are required by farmers to produce goods and services are called …
A. factors of production.
B. demand.
C. capital of production.
D. supply.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - factors of production (2 marks)
The factors of production are land, labour, capital and management (entrepreneurship).

subQuestions.questionText:
Expenses, such as electricity, that are NOT related to one particular enterprise are known as … costs.
A. overhead
B. fixed
C. variable
D. gross
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - overhead (2 marks)
Overhead costs are shared expenses (electricity, telephone, administration) that cannot be allocated to a single enterprise.

subQuestions.questionText:
A plan of action by the farmer to recognise and deal with risks:
A. Risk anticipation
B. Strategic risk management
C. Contingency planning
D. Risk-taking
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Strategic risk management (2 marks)
Strategic risk management is the deliberate, long-term plan of action to identify and deal with risks before they harm the business.

subQuestions.questionText:
The Unemployment Insurance Act, 2001 (Act 63 of 2001) regulates the following:
(i) Employer and employee both contribute towards the fund
(ii) Provision of security for workers should they become unemployed
(iii) Protection of workers from unfair discrimination
(iv) The effects of unemployment for the employee
Choose the CORRECT combination:
A. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
B. (i), (iii) and (iv)
C. (i), (ii) and (iii)
D. (i), (ii) and (iv)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - (i), (ii) and (iv) (2 marks)
The UIF is funded by contributions from both employer and employee and provides income security against the effects of unemployment. Protection from unfair discrimination (iii) is covered by the Employment Equity Act.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following statement about heritability is NOT CORRECT:
A. Genes influence heritability of a characteristic.
B. The environment influences the heritability of a characteristic.
C. A proportion of physical visible differences from parents are passed on to the offspring.
D. Compares similar characteristics among related individuals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - The environment influences the heritability of a characteristic (2 marks)
Heritability is the proportion of variation due to genes. The environment affects the phenotype, but heritability itself is a measure of the genetic contribution.

options.A: Genes influence heritability of a characteristic.
options.B: The environment influences the heritability of a characteristic.
options.C: A proportion of physical visible differences from parents are passed on to the offspring.
options.D: Compares similar characteristics among related individuals.

subQuestions.questionText:
ONE of the following is a possible gene combination that can be produced by an individual with the AaBb genotype during the formation of the gametes:
A. Aa, Bb, AA, ab
B. AA, aa, BB, bb
C. AB, Ab, aB, ab
D. AB, ab, BB, aa
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - AB, Ab, aB, ab (2 marks)
Each gamete carries one allele from each gene pair. An AaBb individual can form four gamete types: AB, Ab, aB and ab.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Placing stickers on products to promote them as environmentally friendly.
COLUMN B options: A. supply  B. economic characteristic  C. diversification  D. eco-labelling  E. qualitative  F. green labelling  G. quantitative  H. land  I. specialisation  J. demand
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D - eco-labelling (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The chain that includes manufacturing and distribution of the product for the market.
COLUMN B options: A. supply  B. economic characteristic  C. diversification  D. eco-labelling  E. qualitative  F. green labelling  G. quantitative  H. land  I. specialisation  J. demand
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: A - supply (supply chain) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The space that is available for agricultural activities.
COLUMN B options: A. supply  B. economic characteristic  C. diversification  D. eco-labelling  E. qualitative  F. green labelling  G. quantitative  H. land  I. specialisation  J. demand
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: H - land (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The strategy through which the farmer can spread the investment over several enterprises.
COLUMN B options: A. supply  B. economic characteristic  C. diversification  D. eco-labelling  E. qualitative  F. green labelling  G. quantitative  H. land  I. specialisation  J. demand
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: C - diversification (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a term/phrase from COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A characteristic that takes on a whole range of values, without clear boundaries between the different classes.
COLUMN B options: A. supply  B. economic characteristic  C. diversification  D. eco-labelling  E. qualitative  F. green labelling  G. quantitative  H. land  I. specialisation  J. demand
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: G - quantitative (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
Changes in price due to seasonality of agricultural products.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Price fluctuation (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
The difference between the value of assets and the value of liabilities.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Net worth (also: net value / owner's equity) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
The scientific study of how genes and traits are passed on to the offspring from parents.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Genetics (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
A type of mutation with one or more extra or missing chromosomes in the set.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Aneuploidy (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
The physical location of a gene on a chromosome.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Locus (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word to make the statement TRUE:
Mass market focuses on a specific product to satisfy specific needs of a market.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Niche (market) (1 mark)
A niche market targets a specific, narrow segment. A mass market targets the whole market with a single offer.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word to make the statement TRUE:
Planning is the management principle which involves the checking and verification of results or goals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Control (monitoring) (1 mark)
Control compares actual results with the plan. Planning is deciding in advance what to do.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word to make the statement TRUE:
A Mendelian square is a table that shows how genetic characteristics are inherited from each parent and the possible genotypes of the offspring.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Punnett (square) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word to make the statement TRUE:
The random change in the genetic composition of a cell is known as variation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Mutation (1 mark)
A random change in the genetic material is a mutation. Variation is the differences among individuals of a species.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word to make the statement TRUE:
A dihybrid has two identical alleles for a particular gene.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Homozygote (homozygous / pure-bred) (1 mark)
An organism with two identical alleles for a gene is a homozygote. A dihybrid is heterozygous for two gene pairs.

questions.title: Section B, Question 2: Agricultural Management and Marketing

subQuestions.questionText:
The supply of products may be more or less than the required quantities in a market. At times the market might be at equilibrium.
State the situation in a market when the products supplied are fewer than the products demanded.
subQuestions.memoText: Shortage (under-supply / deficit). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE factor that could have led to the situation in QUESTION 2.1.1 (a shortage).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• High production costs
• Lack of / outdated technology
• Lack of subsidies
• High demand for the product
• Adverse environmental conditions
• Many competitive products
• A wide range of complementary products
• Expectations of future price changes
• A low price of the product
• Fewer producers
• Production out of season
• Political / market instability
• Legislation

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the situation in a market when it is at equilibrium.
subQuestions.memoText: Market equilibrium is a situation in a market where the quantity demanded (1 mark) is equal to the quantity supplied (1 mark), so the price is stable. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
A method of promoting a product is shown in the question paper: a poster reading 'SPECIAL NOW ON! Only the cheapest, healthiest, most tender and tastiest meat!!'
Indicate the method of promoting products shown above.
subQuestions.memoText: Advertisement (advertising). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO other methods of promoting products.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO (1 mark each): in-store promotion; direct mailing / internet selling; personal selling; trade fairs and exhibitions.

subQuestions.questionText:
An avocado producer sold 500 bags of avocadoes at R50 each, while a maize producer sold 800 bags of maize at R300 each, and both were sold out. Due to high demand, prices went up: a bag of avocadoes was then sold at R55 and a bag of maize at R500. The number of avocado buyers declined from 500 to 250, while maize buyers declined from 800 to 790.
Identify the product that showed price inelasticity of demand.
subQuestions.memoText: Maize (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason to support the answer to QUESTION 2.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText: The large change in the price of maize (R300 to R500) had very little influence on the quantity demanded (800 down to only 790), which is the definition of inelastic demand. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the availability of substitute products contributes to price elasticity of demand.
subQuestions.memoText: When substitute products are available, consumers switch to the cheaper substitute if the price rises, so demand for the product is more elastic. When there are no substitutes, consumers must keep buying it, so demand is more inelastic. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
A schematic representation in the question paper shows the main agricultural marketing functions: A – safekeeping of products in a cool place (storage); B – changing of products to a more usable form (processing); C – (packaging); D – (a fourth main function).
Identify the agricultural marketing function represented by D.
subQuestions.memoText: Transportation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO advantages of the marketing function in B (processing / value adding).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Increases the value of the product (value adding)
• Overcomes over-supply of the product
• Allows easier packaging, handling and transport / convenience
• Provides job opportunities
• Ensures the availability of the product throughout the year
• Reduces spoilage / perishability / longer shelf life
• Ensures food security
• Improves food safety
• Makes the product more appealing to the consumer

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE guideline that farmers should consider to ensure that the safety of products is maintained when performing the marketing function in C (packaging).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Containment for convenient handling
• Prevention of harmful microbial growth
• Free from chemicals / foreign objects / avoid health risks
• Protection against mechanical damage

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the price and demand of sheep over six months.
Month | Price (R) | Demand of sheep
September | 100 | 1 500
October | 120 | 1 500
November | 200 | 1 600
December | 1 050 | 2 000
January | 100 | 1 300
February | 80 | 1 400
Draw a bar graph to show the relationship between the price and demand of sheep over the six-month period.
subQuestions.memoText:
Bar graph. Marking rubric (1 mark each):
• Correct heading
• X-axis correctly calibrated and labelled (Months)
• Y-axis correctly calibrated and labelled (Price and demand of sheep)
• Correct unit (R)
• Bar graph (paired bars for price and demand per month)
• Accuracy (80%+ correctly plotted); December shows the highest price bar (R1 050) and the highest demand bar (2 000)
subQuestions.topic: Agricultural Marketing - Supply and Demand Graphs

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the month in which the farmer had the highest income from the sales of sheep.
subQuestions.memoText: December (price R1 050 × demand 2 000 gives by far the highest income). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the factor that could have led to the higher demand for sheep in December.
subQuestions.memoText: The festive season (increased consumer spending / celebrations at year-end). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the marketing channel associated with the statement:
The farmer sells eggs on the farm.
subQuestions.memoText: Farm-gate marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the marketing channel associated with the statement:
Fruit and vegetables are sold by an agent at the municipal market.
subQuestions.memoText: Fresh produce market (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the marketing channel associated with the statement:
Products are electronically advertised and sold.
subQuestions.memoText: Internet / online marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
An illustration in the question paper shows the phases of the entrepreneurial process in sequence: (A) → prepare an operational plan (B) → mobilise resources → actions to serve the market (C).
Identify the phases of the entrepreneurial process represented by A and B in the illustration.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Identify an opportunity / generate a business idea (1 mark)
B - Plan the business / develop a business plan (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Define the concept entrepreneurship.
subQuestions.memoText: Entrepreneurship is the process of bringing together resources and assets (1 mark) to make use of an opportunity to create a business venture (1 mark). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
A business plan is needed before a business is started.
Indicate TWO aspects that potential investors look for in a business plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Financial viability / the financial plan of the business
• Possible threats and strengths of the business (SWOT analysis)
• The marketing plan
• The human resource plan

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO electronic resources that can be used as tools for drawing up a business plan.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO (1 mark each): computers / cell phones / laptops; computer software programmes; Wi-Fi connections / data.

subQuestions.label: 3.1.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
The economic characteristics of land as a production factor are: availability; appreciation; law of diminishing returns; collateral; specific environment.
Match the following statement with one of these economic characteristics:
(a) The price of land tends to increase over time.
subQuestions.memoText: Appreciation (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.1.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Match the following statement with one of the economic characteristics of land (availability; appreciation; law of diminishing returns; collateral; specific environment):
(b) Land is a valuable asset that farmers may use as security for a loan.
subQuestions.memoText: Collateral (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.1.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Explain how the following farming method may be used to increase land productivity:
(a) Use of scientific methods.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE explained (2 marks):
• Farmers make informed decisions based on reliable data about soil conditions, crop health, weather and pests
• Waste and environmental impact are minimised through crop rotation, cover cropping, reduced tillage and precision agriculture
• Resources such as irrigation, fertilisation and pest control are optimally allocated, maximising crop yield

subQuestions.label: 3.1.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Explain how the following farming method may be used to increase land productivity:
(b) Consolidation of small uneconomical land units.
subQuestions.memoText: Combining small units into one larger unit improves the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of investments in transport, communication networks, utilities and irrigation systems, so more can be produced per rand spent. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
A flow chart in the question paper shows methods a farmer used to increase labour productivity: A – buying tractors and harvesters; B – establishing training centres; C – providing condoms and ARVs to employees; D – providing secure houses to farm workers.
Define the concept labour productivity.
subQuestions.memoText: Labour productivity is the production output of the labour force in relation to the amount paid in wages; i.e. a measure of output per unit of labour input. (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the labour problem that is addressed by the farmer in B (establishing training centres).
subQuestions.memoText: Lack of skills / training (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the labour problem that is addressed by the farmer in C (providing condoms and ARVs to employees).
subQuestions.memoText: HIV and AIDS / diseases / absenteeism / scarcity of labourers. (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the labour problem that is addressed by the farmer in D (providing secure houses to farm workers).
subQuestions.memoText: Poor living conditions. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate how the measure in A (buying tractors and harvesters) can increase labour productivity.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): more work is completed in a shorter time; workers work more efficiently; it eliminates fatigue.

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
An extract of the components and items from a contract signed between a farm worker and a farmer:
Component 1 – item: '4 October 2020 to retirement'
Component 2 (JOB TITLE) – item: 'Spray operator'
Component 3 (LEAVE) – item: 'One month paid leave per year'
Component 4 – item: '07:00–17:00 daily'
Component 5 – item: 'Monthly salary/wage'
Component 6 (PROTECTIVE GEAR) – item: 'Overall, mask and gloves'
Indicate the component of the contract represented by 1.
subQuestions.memoText: Term / duration of employment. (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the component of the contract represented by 4 ('07:00–17:00 daily').
subQuestions.memoText: Working hours. (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the component of the contract represented by 5 ('Monthly salary/wage').
subQuestions.memoText: Mode / method of payment (remuneration). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the labour legislation that addresses leave benefits.
subQuestions.memoText: Basic Conditions of Employment Act / BCEA (Act 75 of 1997). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the item in the contract that addresses compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act 85 of 1993).
subQuestions.memoText: Overall, mask and gloves (protective gear). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Three pictures in the question paper represent different capital items on a farm: PICTURE A shows medication for external parasites; PICTURE B shows a movable item (e.g. a tractor / implement); PICTURE C shows a fixed structure (e.g. land / a building).
Identify the type of capital represented in PICTURE C.
subQuestions.memoText: Fixed capital (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of capital represented in PICTURE A (medication for external parasites).
subQuestions.memoText: Production / working / floating capital. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the type of credit that can be used to purchase the capital item in PICTURE B (a movable capital item such as a tractor).
subQuestions.memoText: Medium-term credit: it is used to purchase medium-term (movable) assets and is repayable over a period of about 2 to 10 years. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
A financial record for the period April to July is given in the question paper. It has monthly rows for INCOME (operating income, capital sales, non-farm income), EXPENDITURE (operating, capital, non-farm/bank charges) and a CASH FLOW SUMMARY (opening balance, total income, total expenses, profit/loss, closing balance). For July the total income is R41 200 and the total expenses are R9 500; June's closing balance is R79 100.
The financial record in the table above is NOT an income statement. Give a reason to support the statement.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (2 marks):
• It has a cash flow summary / opening balance / closing balance, which are not components of an income statement
• An income statement shows the dates of transactions, which do not appear in this record
• It records cash items only (an income statement includes non-cash items such as depreciation)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the value of A (the opening balance for July in the cash flow summary).
subQuestions.memoText: A = R79 100 (July's opening balance equals June's closing balance). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.5.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the value of B (the profit or loss for July).
subQuestions.memoText:
B (Profit/Loss) = Total income − Total expenses
= R41 200 − R9 500
= R31 700 (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 3.5.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the value of C (the closing balance for July).
subQuestions.memoText:
C (Closing balance) = Opening balance + Profit/Loss
= R79 100 + R31 700
= R110 800 (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason that supports the viability of the enterprise above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): it is generating a profit / net income is positive (e.g. R31 700 in July); income is higher than expenses every month.

subQuestions.label: 3.6.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A farming enterprise can be influenced by different forces.
Identify the external force represented by: an increase in the VAT on commodities.
subQuestions.memoText: Economic / political force. (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.6.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the external force represented by: new emerging markets for farm products.
subQuestions.memoText: Competition (competitive force). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.6.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the source of risk linked to QUESTION 3.6.1(a) (an increase in the VAT on commodities).
subQuestions.memoText: Financial / market and price risk. (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.6.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the source of risk linked to QUESTION 3.6.1(b) (new emerging markets for farm products).
subQuestions.memoText: Market and price risk. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO general management skills needed to manage a farming business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Labour / land / financial / stock / crisis management
• Conceptual skills
• Analytical skills
• Ability to apply new knowledge
• Problem solving and decision making skills
• Planning skills
• Organisational / co-ordination skills
• Interpersonal and communication skills
• Ability to adapt
• Delegation skills

questions.title: Section B, Question 4: Basic Agricultural Genetics

subQuestions.questionText:
A genetic diagram in the question paper illustrates a cross between a black bull and a white cow (black is dominant). It shows P1 → Process 1 → gametes → F1-generation → Process 2 → gametes → F2-generation.
Name the type of crossing illustrated in the genetic diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText: Monohybrid cross (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 4.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText: It is a cross that involves only one characteristic / trait (coat colour). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.1.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify PROCESS 1 in the genetic diagram above (the step that produces the gametes from the P1 parents).
subQuestions.memoText: Meiosis (gametogenesis). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.1.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify PROCESS 2 in the genetic diagram above (the step that combines gametes to form the F2-generation).
subQuestions.memoText: Fertilisation (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.1.4(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the number of black offspring in the F2-generation (from the monohybrid cross where black is dominant: F1 Bb × Bb).
subQuestions.memoText: 3 (F2 ratio is 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb, so 3 black : 1 white). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.1.4(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the phenotype of the F1-generation (black bull BB × white cow bb).
subQuestions.memoText: All black (all F1 are Bb, and black is dominant). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the genotypic ratio of the F2-generation (from the F1 Bb × Bb cross).
subQuestions.memoText: 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
In pea plants, spherical seeds (D) are dominant over dented seeds (d). Two plants heterozygous for seed shape (Dd) were crossed.
Use a Punnett square to determine the genotype of the F1-generation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Gametes of each parent: D and d.
Punnett square offspring: DD, Dd, Dd, dd.
Marking rubric (1 mark each): correct gametes of the male parent; correct gametes of the female parent; correct genotype of the offspring; populated Punnett square.
F1 genotypic ratio = 1 DD : 2 Dd : 1 dd.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the fraction of the F1-generation that should have spherical seed shape (from the Dd × Dd cross).
subQuestions.memoText: 3/4 (DD, Dd and Dd are spherical; only dd is dented). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Assume that 900 pea plants were produced as the F1-generation. Calculate the number of plants that will have spherical seeds.
subQuestions.memoText:
= 3/4 × 900
= 675 pea plants (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the pattern of inheritance represented by the statement:
A plant with purple flowers is crossed with a plant with white flowers and all offspring have both purple and white colours in the same flower.
subQuestions.memoText: Co-dominance (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the pattern of inheritance represented by the statement:
Milk production is influenced by a combination of many genes.
subQuestions.memoText: Polygenic inheritance (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the pattern of inheritance represented by the statement:
There are four alleles for the C gene that controls coat colour in rabbits.
subQuestions.memoText: Multiple alleles (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the pattern of inheritance represented by the statement:
The development of a grey-coloured calf from the crossing of a white cow with a black bull.
subQuestions.memoText: Incomplete dominance (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A picture in the question paper shows differences between individuals of the same species (a group of animals differing in horn shape, colour, body size and weight).
Identify a characteristic in the animals that is influenced by genetic causes of variation.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): horn conformation / colour / body conformation / size / frame / height / sex / number of ears.

subQuestions.label: 4.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify a characteristic in the animals that is influenced by environmental causes of variation.
subQuestions.memoText: Body weight (mass). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO important aspects (importance) of variation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Forms the foundation for selection
• Allows genetic improvement
• Improves adaptability
• Contributes to food security
• Provides disease resistance
• Allows the development of new breeds / improved biodiversity

subQuestions.label: 4.5.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
An illustration in the question paper shows different breeds on which animal breeders based their selection (parent breeds Sussex, Bonsmara, Nguni and Simmentaler leading to BREED A and BREED B, and then to BREED C, BREED D and BREED E).
Identify the type of breeding system between BREED C and BREED D (closely related animals bred together).
subQuestions.memoText: Inbreeding (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.5.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of selection shown in the illustration above (a breeder deliberately choosing which animals to mate to develop new breeds).
subQuestions.memoText: Artificial selection (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 4.5.1(a).
subQuestions.memoText: It involves the mating of closely related animals. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO disadvantages of the breeding system in QUESTION 4.5.1(a) (inbreeding).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Inbreeding depression / a decrease in the performance of animals
• Leads to the expression of lethal genes / deformities
• Reduced vitality
• Low resistance to diseases
• Poor adaptability
• Loss of variation
• Undesired genes are made homozygous

subQuestions.questionText: Name the method of selection that was used to obtain BREED E, based on the performance of the Nguni and the Bonsmara (the recorded performance of the parent breeds).
subQuestions.memoText: Pedigree selection (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Scientists conducted an experiment to test the effect of genetic modification on insect resistance in maize plants. They planted maize seeds carrying an insect-resistant gene and normal (non-GM) seeds, both in an environment with corn borers.
Formulate a hypothesis based on the experiment.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Genetic modification results in more insect resistance in maize plants
• Genetic modification results in less insect resistance in maize plants
• Genetic modification has no impact on insect resistance in maize plants

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO socio-economic impacts of genetically modified maize seeds on small-scale farmers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• They cannot afford GM seeds because they are expensive
• GM crops are protected by patent, so farmers may not retain seed for planting
• GM crops may be engineered to be sterile, forcing farmers to buy new seed each season

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of genetic modification over traditional methods.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO (1 mark each): it is fast; it is precise; it is not limited to organisms of the same species.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO aims of the genetic modification of plants and animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Improving crop yield
• Improving commercial properties / shelf life / flavour
• Increasing the nutritional value of crops (biofortification)
• Producing pharmaceutical crops
• Improving desirable characteristics
• Producing industrial or consumer products
• Developing animal models for the study of diseases
• Increasing product quality
• Increasing resistance to diseases and pests
• Improving tolerance to environmental conditions
• Producing products for human therapeutic use
• Improving herbicide resistance
